title: How are ya'll handling the Steam AI self disclosure?
author: BladesBurden
selftext:
I just went with a generic "Yeah, I used AI" statement, as listing out details just feels exhausting at this point:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2783100/Blades_Burden/

I figure if someone is against AI enough, I really don't need to waste my time explaining that I used it for some equipment icons, or a random town map, because any genAI usage at all is automatically a disqualification for some people (which they're obviously allowed to feel that way).

But I still got asked on occasion what I used it for, which then makes me feel like I'm obligated to source every asset or technique used in the design of my game, on the spot, so that someone can determine if my project is "pure enough". And after I've done that, I've even had accusations of non-AI, commissioned artwork, being genAI when it's not 🤷 

So yeah, I'm wondering how ya'll are going about it, and what kind of responses you're getting on your released projects.

comments.author: NikkiWebster
comments.body:
There is some amount of stigma around AI, but I think the best option is open honesty. 

If you are vague, people will make up their own beliefs and base their opinion on that. If you are specific, then I think that will result in a better perception.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
Isn't saying bluntly that I've used genAI the more honest way to approach that?

The whole trend of saying "I used GenAI to create art/music/models and then meretriciously curated them with a human touch to make them match the games theme" just feels like 500 words to say "I used GenAI".

I guess I could detail out in vague terms "Used for some art XY but not Z. Used for soundfx AB but not C. etc." but at that point, it just feels like a laundry list that I'll have to keep updating as I replace AI placeholders or add more into the game.

I think I'd rather rule out any hard anti-AI users right off the bat rather than try to pull in the occasional "I'm OK with AI music but not art" people.

replies.author: NikkiWebster
replies.body:
I think if I read a generic "I used GenAI" my mind would jump to the assumption that the game was visecoded and probably low effort. 

If you outlined that it was used for background art, voice acting, etc. whatever you actually used it for, I would be more inclined to believe it wasn't AI slop but instead used AI as a tool. 

There will be some people that see any AI and will ignore the game regardless, but some people, myself included, will give it more consideration if I feel like the dev is communicating openly and honestly.

replies.author: Mundane_Background19
replies.body:
Did you really look this word up just for this post?

**Meretricious**

(pronounced *mer-uh-TRISH-us*) is a formal adjective meaning superficially attractive or flashy, yet lacking real value, substance, or sincerity. It can also mean based on pretense or deception, and in older or specialized contexts, it relates to prostitution or non-marital sexual relationships.

replies.author: mugsy342
replies.body: I know it’s a bit of a guess, but I think confidence with the transparency is key. For one, hiding it at all can leave even a tiny crumb to jump on as seen recently, but I think being clear and open from the start, but unwavering, is my bet. A big advantage being small/new is you get to set your identity. The bigger and/or older groups have a harder time with that because they have a preexisting identity they are being judged against/to a lot of times, hence why so many of them hide it now and tiptoe around it. Start strong and clear and that gives you a better opportunity to continue with that same brand attitude. And make sure your product can speak for itself, no amount of identity or marketing can save a bad product at your scale(that’s the downside of being new/small)

comments.author: Nebuchadnezzar_z
comments.body: In a year (maybe less) every one will be using AI and will have to disclose it. I am certain no one is coding completely manually any more. It's the AI art that's still a sticky point, and that will change eventually too. I remember when seeing AI art in real life (posters, menus, etc) at first would go eww AI.. now it's normal.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body: Yeah. Working full-time in the software industry, outside of gamedev, it feels insane to think any large game is being made right now without using AI. But I don't expect we'll see an AI disclosure when GTA6 makes its way to steam 😂

replies.author: Advice2Anyone
replies.body: Even if you can why the hell would you, like even before ai everyone was just grabbing repos and stringing them together for a lot of stuff it cuts so much time down between hunting for stuff and tweaking.

replies.author: Maphreal
replies.body: Hell before ai was accessible to the general public, people were selling ai generated paintings as a novelty, and it seemed they sold decent. Most of what I saw leaned into the hallucinations for some surrealism. Wasn't until all the low effort furry porn artists lost their free lunch that it fell out of favor on the net.

comments.author: BSwayzeYo
comments.body: Disclose it. It sucks but just do it. Thats how to handle it. There are plenty of people who will pay for a great game regardless of how it is made. Those people are ignoring the ai hate-mob. You and I and everyone else should to.

comments.author: RegioMamalon666
comments.body:
I think you're doing a disservice to tour potential audience to just being vage.

I do browse steam regularly and still trying to adapt to this AI nonsense, im not fully against AI since its use is inevitable but I use it (along other criteria) to decide if I should bother engaging more with the steam page.

What users are actually trying to infer is what to expect in the "user facing content".

If I scan quickly the ai disclosure and find it was mostly icons or minor/secondary assets I'll just "okay-it" and keep watching the page.

If I see major ai usage like music, character portraits, backgrounds and the like then I skip it.

Some of us have actual critical thinking and just want to know what to expect from a game

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
> If I scan quickly the ai disclosure and find it was mostly icons or minor/secondary assets I'll just "okay-it" and keep watching the page.

That's fair. I guess the question is if I want to cater to everyone's individual stance on AI usage or not. There are plenty of artists out there that would have the exact opposite thoughts as you (e.g. Music is OK, but icons are not), I guess being more detailed about it could make some people happier if my usage fits their specific views on AI, but I'm still not sure if I want to go down that path as it just opens me up to more accusations if I end up missing an asset here or there.

comments.author: Navadvisor
comments.body: Do what the triple A's do that make the disclosure, AI may have been used with coding and assets blah blah. Generic, you should be able to find several examples.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
Got any examples off the top of your head? I can't think of a single AAA game with an AI disclosure.

I could name a few that got in trouble for not disclosing it. But then they just replace the assets and still don't have a disclosure up.

replies.author: NoAccountant6665
replies.body: Both the Finals and Arc Raiders are known for the usage of AI voiceover. Both games have the disclosure and are doing great.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
Oh nice, they do!

Seems like they went with a similar approach to a lot of the comments here with the (paraphrased) "We used AI, but the end result is a work of the development team / humans involved".

replies.author: Navadvisor
replies.body: Man I don't have it handy someone posted it here a while back

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body: It's all good. NoAccountant6665 posted some examples as a reply.

replies.author: PwnCall
replies.body: New call of duty has the disclosure

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body: Huh, interesting. Wasn't expecting that one. And even more interesting, it looks like they went with a vague "GenAI was used" statement.

replies.author: PwnCall
replies.body: It’s easier to assume it’s on everything than to assume it’s not on everything from now on.

comments.author: CubeUnleashed
comments.body:
Mine was "*Generative AI was used to create various graphical assets featured in the game. These assets were selected, edited, composited and integrated by the developer as part of the game’s visual design, alongside substantial human creative direction, implementation and refinement.*"  
When an Anti AI Curator added it to their "Avoid these games"-List they just wrote: Developer says Generative AI was used to create various graphical assets featured in the game.

Someone who is fundamentally against AI probably won't change their mind because I explain my workflow in three paragraphs. But idk, it's important to me, at least in the current landscape around indie games and AI, to give context.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
> Mine was "Generative AI was used to create various graphical assets featured in the game. These assets were selected, edited, composited and integrated by the developer as part of the game’s visual design, alongside substantial human creative direction, implementation and refinement."

In the other (non-ai) gamedev subs, this is kind of a joke/meme they post, because it just comes off as "I used AI, but I'm trying to make it sound like I didn't".

I don't disagree that this is exactly how I, and a lot of people here likely do use AI. But it feels performative to word things like that, even if it's honest. (That said, its still probably the best approach for the time being 🤷).

replies.author: CubeUnleashed
replies.body: Doesn't feel performative to me but I get what you mean. For future projects maybe I'll try the "yes, AI was used" approach. There are fewer and fewer people having a problem with AI in game dev anyways.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
Performative might not even be the right word for me to use there.

I suppose the biggest problem with that style is that there's nothing stopping anyone from 100% vibecoding a game in a single prompt, and putting up a description like that anyway.

If everyone is wording their disclosures with the "heavily human influenced" approach, then it's hard to take any of them seriously.

Again, at this current point in time, you're probably on the right path there. But I feel like a year from now, that will be more of a "Yeah, we've heard that one before." approach to disclosures for most gamers.

comments.author: buzzspinner
comments.body: Being honest about using it. Damned if you do damned if you dont

comments.author: shadow_fen
comments.body: Disclose it... I'm against AI images but I'm fine with AI code, so if you're ambiguous you're gonna get people assuming the worst

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body: Hate to break it to you, but you have most likely already played games with AI images and you couldn't tell the difference. Not trying to be confrontational, but it's just going to get better so you might as well get used to it

comments.author: Professor_Snipe
comments.body: If the game is good/polished, even if slop heavy, people seem not to care (Path of Idle/Warpack come to mind). If the game is mediocre and heavy on the AI department, you're utterly fucked.

comments.author: Hot_Masterpiece_3668
comments.body: This game looks full AI dude.   Are people really going to buy that?

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
It's still a large work in progress, but I'm interested to hear where you think the AI usage is.

I'll share my list afterwards.

replies.author: AdminClown
replies.body: Your third steam picture, the Blade Keep map is the standard default look of AI generated imagery. That look is synonymous with AI slop projects because its the style that AI generations default to when not specified or polished and can give the impression that you didn't even try.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body: Yep, that's surely one of them. Have no intention of keeping it in the released game, but also needed something to map out my town features that are constantly changing.

replies.author: AdminClown
replies.body: I understand but in the current game dev environment 1 first impression is everything you get. Putting placeholders featured so centrally is a big detriment to that.

replies.author: BladesBurden
replies.body:
Hmm, yeah. Good point.

Guess I wasn't too concerned since I'm still a ways away from "wishlist gathering" time. And the keep upgrading is a big part of the game which is why I originally threw it up there. But you're probably right on not showing that yet.

comments.author: Automatic-Garbage976
comments.body:
I'm convinced that from this point forward in history, no game will be developed without the assistance of ai.

I mean sure, there are still people making their own tools from ore they gathered, and there will still be coders clinging to the glory days for nostalgia sake, but every commercial product is going to be kissed by ai in some way or another

comments.author: Polyxeno
comments.body: Looking forward to saying no AI was used. :-)

comments.author: revolutionPanda
comments.body: Just waiting until the anti-ai hate and disclaimers are still around. I'll keep working on my game without showing it until then.

comments.author: NeusomaDev
comments.body: I haven’t shipped so massive grain of salt, but as a consumer that had to come around on this issue before I started trying to make stuff, I tend to agree with your read. If your game looks like slop, it doesn’t matter how much you try to explain or rationalize, you’re gonna get clowned and arguably it’s deserved. If it looks great, very few people will care about the particulars. Regardless, the particulars are generally a way for bad faith actors to waste your time (the old “it’s faster to make an accusation than rebut it” trick), so don’t agonize over it. If people seem to care, it’s probably because they think your game is slop or slop-adjacent, and a detailed statement isn’t gonna move the needle.

comments.author: redskeletonbarbarian
comments.body: I just remind myself that making a game takes more effort than filling out a form and I just fill it out

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: Don't disclose how will anyone prove it?

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body: I'm very clear and transparent about my use of AI and the reasons behind it. If people react to it, so be it. I think it's worse to lie and get caught, specially if your game looks 100% AI. On devblogs I'm very transparent: I'm creating my own stuff + using AI and free assets where it makes sense; if I get the budget/money, I'd be more than happy to invest in custom assets (graphical, sound, music, etc.).
